prompt_version: s5-extract-facts-v2 (adapted from Paleo Atlas extract-facts-v3; v2 after Sofía's S5 review)

facts.statement: The study involved 587 adults between the ages of 18 and 89 who filled out the Italian version of the Cognitive Reserve Scale.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The researchers created a shorter seven-item version of the scale, checked its basic reliability, and created reference percentiles for the scores.
facts.subject: other

facts.statement: The seven-item version showed acceptable internal consistency and explained 31.60% of the variance in the data.
facts.subject: other

facts.statement: Scores on the new short form were strongly associated with the original full scale and moderately associated with the Montreal Cognitive Assessment.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Statistical testing supported that the average scores on the short form were equivalent to the original scale within set limits.
facts.subject: other

facts.statement: The authors suggest the new measure is promising because it may reduce the effort required from participants while still aligning with the original tool.
facts.subject: other
